faqs.q: Can we go straight into Silver, Gold or Platinum without the earlier courses?
faqs.a: Yes for Silver and Gold, if your dog is already at the right obedience level — Gaynor judges that with a conversation, asking what your dog can already do, rather than a formal assessment. Platinum is different: it isn't open to direct entry, since it's the highest stage and entirely off lead. Gold graduates discuss moving up to it with Gaynor at graduation, once there are enough of them to form a class.

faqs.q: How do the awards work, what if we don't pass, and where do we pick up after a gap?
faqs.a: Each week you learn something new, and in week six Gaynor reviews everything from the course. Get it all right and you earn that course's rosette; not quite, and you get an "achievement" rosette instead — you can still move up, and pick up the full rosette once you've got it on the next course. Coming back after a gap of months or years, most dogs restart on Bronze, but if you've kept the training up you may be able to start higher — ring for a chat and Gaynor will help you judge it. Platinum is the highest of the group courses; after that, Gaynor works one to one with dogs and owners on whatever they want to take further.
